title: Microsoft Teams: emoji shortcuts with autocomplete on iOS and Android
summary: The rollout, default and shortcut behaviours match Microsoft's notice and roadmap. The upload-policy path omits Edit, and the prose wrongly casts tenant-wide custom emoji controls as unconfirmed for mobile; it also says nothing happens without a colon despite documenting parenthesis shortcuts.

claims.claim: Uploaded custom emojis are accessible to all users in the tenant alongside standard emojis.
claims.quote: These emojis and reactions are also accessible to all users in the tenant alongside the standard Teams emojis and reactions.

claims.claim: The tenant custom emoji switch is at Teams admin center > Messaging Settings > Custom emojis > use custom emojis.
claims.quote: In the Teams Admin Center controls, go to Messaging Settings section and toggle the use custom emojis option, found under the Custom emojis section, on or off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMessagingConfiguration -CustomEmojis $false disables custom emojis and reactions across the tenant.
claims.quote:
Set-CsTeamsMessagingConfiguration -CustomEmojis $False
The command shown in example 1 disables custom emojis within Teams.
This setting enables/disables the use of custom emojis and reactions across the whole tenant.

claims.claim: Upload custom emojis can be configured at Teams admin center > Messaging policies > policy > Upload custom emojis.
claims.quote: Select the policy by clicking to the left of the policy name, and then select Edit.
claims.fix: Replace controls[2].ui.path and the rendered path with 'Messaging policies > policy > Edit > Upload custom emojis'. Keep the existing surface and docs URL.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMessagingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -CreateCustomEmojis $false disables creation for that policy's users.
claims.quote:
[-CreateCustomEmojis <Boolean>]
This setting enables the creation of custom emojis and reactions within an organization for the specified policy users.
Identity for the teams messaging policy you're modifying.

claims.claim: Uploading custom emojis is on by default.
claims.quote: Upload custom emojis - Set which users can create custom emojis. This setting is on by default.

claims.claim: Upload custom emojis governs creation for policy users, rather than their ability to insert existing custom emojis.
claims.quote:
These emojis and reactions are also accessible to all users in the tenant alongside the standard Teams emojis and reactions.
Set which users can create new emojis via the Messaging Policy groups

claims.claim: The correctly documented tenant custom emoji control is not documented as covering the mobile shortcut menu.
claims.quote: This setting enables/disables the use of custom emojis and reactions across the whole tenant.
claims.fix: Replace controls[1].note and its rendered note with 'Existing custom emoji control; on by default. Enables or disables use of custom emojis and reactions across the whole tenant.' The documented reach includes custom emojis used through mobile shortcuts, without turning off standard emoji shortcuts.

claims.claim: It is unconfirmed whether the tenant custom emoji control restricts custom emojis used through mobile shortcuts.
claims.quote: This setting enables/disables the use of custom emojis and reactions across the whole tenant.
claims.fix: Replace the sentence beginning 'Neither the notice nor the custom emoji page' with 'The tenant setting enables or disables use of custom emojis and reactions across the whole tenant; the Upload custom emojis policy setting controls creation, not insertion.' Remove the first Open questions bullet. Keep the distinction that these are not switches for standard emoji shortcuts.

claims.claim: Teams messaging policies include a Delete custom emojis setting.
claims.quote: The Messaging policies section of the Teams admin center will allow you to turn the Upload custom emojis and Delete custom emojis settings on or off.

claims.claim: Delete custom emojis is off by default except for Teams admins.
claims.quote: Delete custom emojis - Set which users can delete custom emojis. This setting is off by default (except for Teams admins).
